examples.sourceTitle: Xbox Wire — Escape from the Ginso Tree

en.observation: Rising water turns the route into a forced upward scroll: the player must keep climbing and use Bash before the lower part of the screen is flooded.
The finale is won by surviving Kuro’s passes and completing the burning route; forward progress replaces damage to a health bar.
Kuro repeatedly enters the route from outside the playable lane, making the edge of the screen an attack origin instead of a neutral border.

examples.sourceTitle: Ori and the Will of the Wisps — All Bosses

en.observation: Howl’s full-body pounce crosses horizontal space and commits the boss to a readable line, giving the player a clear dodge decision.

examples.game: Ori and the Will of the Wisps

en.observation: A ground pound sends a wave along the floor, separating the boss’s impact point from the threat that travels toward the player.

examples.game: Ori and the Will of the Wisps

en.observation: The beetle commits to its charge and follow-up head impact, creating a stable trajectory that the player can read and route around.

examples.game: Ori and the Will of the Wisps

en.observation: The vulnerable glowing rear concentrates the damage window behind the boss and makes crossing through or over it part of the attack puzzle.

examples.game: Ori and the Will of the Wisps

en.observation: After a charge or heavy landing, the beetle is briefly stunned, turning the end of its attack into a bounded counterattack window.

examples.game: Ori and the Will of the Wisps
examples.sourceTitle: Game Developer — Crafting Mora’s multi-phase score

en.observation: The encounter changes from a first arena phase into a chase transition and then a final arena, so the phase boundary also changes the player’s immediate objective.

examples.game: Ori and the Will of the Wisps

en.observation: Shriek fires a spread of projectiles whose gaps are both dodge lanes and potential launch directions for Bash.

examples.game: Ori and the Will of the Wisps

en.observation: Bash turns an incoming projectile into movement and a redirected shot, so the same object alternates between threat and counterattack resource.

examples.game: Ori and the Will of the Wisps

en.observation: Shriek can leave the arena and return in a horizontal pass, turning an off-screen side into the origin of the next attack.

examples.game: Ori and the Will of the Wisps

en.observation: A mark at the side of the screen warns where Shriek’s horizontal pass will enter, communicating direction before the boss becomes visible.

examples.game: Ori and the Will of the Wisps

en.observation: Later attacks destroy the ground and force Ori to stay airborne, converting a stable arena into a movement system built from falling projectiles.
